messages.subject: WORKSHOPS: Distance sampling, Canada, March-April 2004
parts:
DISTANCE SAMPLING WORKSHOPS
Ontario, Canada
March 31st-April 7th 2004

1st ANNOUNCEMENT
PRELIMINARY REGISTRATION OPEN


http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance.workshops.canada/

The Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling (CREEM) is
presenting two linked workshops in the spring of 2004 in Ontario, Canada. The
aim of these workshops is to train participants in the latest methods for design
and analysis of distance sampling surveys, including line and point transects.
The workshops are taught by leading researchers in the field, using industry-
standard software.

The first workshop will run at an introductory level, and will focus on
"conventional" distance sampling methods, as described in the standard reference
book Introduction to Distance Sampling. The workshop will be a blend of theory
and practice and participants will learn how to use the program Distance.
Participants will gain a solid grounding in both survey design and methods of
analysis for distance sampling surveys.

The second workshop will cover the latest advances in distance sampling research
and software. It is intended for those already familiar with conventional
distance sampling methods. Participants will learn the use of covariates for
modelling the detection function, double-platform methods for when detection at
the line or point is not certain, spatial modelling of density, automated survey
design and adaptive sampling. Participants will learn the more advanced
features of Distance, and some practical sessions will use the free statistical
software R.

For both workshops, participants are encouraged to bring their own data sets,
and can expect to do some preliminary analyses with their data.

The workshops are being hosted by the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources at
the Leslie M. Frost Natural Resources Centre, Dorset, Ontario. With its
wonderful lakeside location, surrounded by pristine forest, the centre provides
a fantastic setting for our workshops. Transport from Toronto (Pearson)
International Airport to the Frost Centre is part of the workshop package.

The number of participants on each workshop is limited to 35. Places will be
filled on a first-come, first-served basis on receipt of completed registration
form and payment in full. Judging from previous years' workshops we expect to
fill all the places, we encourage you to register early!

We are currently in the final stages of working out the registration
arrangements, and hope to open registration in a few weeks. Meanwhile, if you
are interested in coming, we encourage you to register interest by contacting
the workshop organizer (address below).

For more information, see the workshop web pages:
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance.workshops.canada/
which are also accessable by following links from the CREEM web site
http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/
